title: Verify taskset line
description: One task of a Verify taskset. A taskset is JSON lines: one object per line, no enclosing array, UTF-8. Submitted as the taskset blob of VerifyRun, VerifyGenerate and (as the generators) VerifyGenerateAndCheck. The controller accepts exactly what this schema allows: a line with a field that is not listed here (a misspelt one is such a field), with a field or a source name given twice, with a value of another type (null included) or a number outside its range is refused, by the field's name. Beyond what a schema can say: every string must be valid Unicode (half of a surrogate pair written as an escape is refused); a line is at most 67108864 bytes (64 MiB); a task's text (its sources with their names, its arguments, its inputs and expected outputs) is at most 8388608 characters (8 MiB); a taskset has at most 4194304 tasks, each index once. A taskset with a line that is refused, an unknown runtime id or a task that is too large is refused whole when it is split; the preflight says so beforehand, by line, name or index, in a bounded number of messages.

index.description: The task's index in the report. Defaults to the line's ordinal. No two tasks of a taskset have one index.

runtime.description: A runtime id from the controller's catalog, to the letter (ids are case-sensitive): python-3.14.6, python-3.14.6-sympy-1.14.0, python-3.14.6-numpy-2.5.4 (numpy built in; its default integer is 32-bit, use dtype=np.int64 for 64-bit integers; no BLAS, threads or SIMD), quickjs-0.15.1, typescript-sucrase-3.35.1 (TypeScript, the types stripped by sucrase, no type check), ruby-3.4.1, lua-5.4.8 (the sources are files in a read-only folder that is the guest's whole file system: the entry is Lua's script, require finds a neighbour), clang-22.1.0 (C17 and C++20 without exceptions, compiled on the node under its own budget: .c, .cc, .cpp, .cxx sources are compiled and linked, headers sit beside them; the program runs as a raw WASI module), or wasi (the entry is itself a WASI command module, compiled from Rust, C/C++, Zig, TinyGo or anything else that targets wasm32-wasi; at most 8 MiB, and compiling it is paid from the task's fuel). A taskset that names an unknown id is refused when it is split, and the preflight reports it as not well formed.

entry.description: The source file to run: one of the source names. Defaults to the first source. For the wasi runtime, the module file; its name is the guest's argv[0].

sources.description: File name → file content, at most 1024 files. For the python, quickjs, typescript and ruby runtimes the entry is the program, passed inline; for lua and clang every source is a file in a read-only folder; for the wasi runtime the entry is the module's bytes in base64 (a preflight rejects anything else). A content may not hold a NUL character (U+0000): a program is handed to its interpreter as a C string, and one would cut it. A name must be portable, whatever the runtime: the characters A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - +, folders separated by '/', at most 128 bytes in all and 8 segments. Beyond what the pattern says: no '.' or '..' segment, no segment that ends with '.', none that Windows reserves for a device (CON, NUL, COM1, ...), no two names that differ only in case, and no name that is a file and a folder of another. A taskset with another name is refused when it is split, by the name.

args.description: Arguments after the entry (Python: sys.argv[1:]; wasi: argv[1:]), at most 1024. An argument may not hold a NUL character.

stdin.description: Standard input for a run without a suite. Any text, a NUL character included: it reaches the program as bytes.

seed.description: Seed of the sandbox's deterministic random source (WASI random_get). Default 0. Every seed has a stream of its own. Seed 0 keeps the stream it always had; the stream of every other seed changed in 0.13.0 (seeds 2k and 2k+1 used to share one).

suite.description: Test cases, at most 1024. The task runs once a case, each run under the task's limits, and passes when every case passes; the first failing case sets the verdict. The cases share the task's stdout cap. An empty array is a task without a suite.

args.description: Appended to the task's args for this case; at most 1024, none with a NUL character.

expected_stdout.description: The exact stdout of a passing case; absent = only the exit code counts.

expected_exit.description: The exit code of a passing case. A case passes only when the program ended by itself (it returned or called exit) with this code: a crash is not an exit, so -1 does not pass on one. A case that is met passes whatever the program wrote to stderr. A non-zero exit where 0 was expected is a RuntimeError; any other mismatch of a run that ended by itself is a Fail.

limits.description: Per-task limits; omitted fields take the job defaults, and every field is clamped to the ceilings (fuel 240e9, memory 2 GiB, stdout 8 MiB, stderr 1 MiB) when the taskset is split and again on the node. A task with a suite runs once a case, each run under these limits.

fuel.description: wasmtime fuel: one unit an instruction, and one a byte a call into the host moves. The one budget of a run's work: Timeout means out of fuel. Default 20e9, about ten seconds of a busy loop on a slow machine.

memory.description: Linear memory cap in bytes; default 256 MiB.

wall_ms.description: Deprecated. Accepted and not a limit since 0.13.0: a run is bounded by its fuel, and the wall clock is a node's own backstop that gives no verdict. There is no default and no ceiling; the preflight says so with one message when a taskset sets it.

stdout_bytes.description: Cap on the stdout the task keeps, all cases of a suite together; default 256 KiB. The write that passes it ends the run: OutputExceeded.

stderr_bytes.description: Captured stderr cap; default 64 KiB. Past it stderr is dropped and flagged, and the run goes on.
